DIN 3861 covers the 24° cone cutting ring and DIN 3870 the matching retaining nut, in light (L) and heavy (S) series. No test certificate is attached to the listing; tell us the documents your project needs when you ask for a quotation.

faqs.q: What does the Retaining Nut, DIN 3870 Heavy Series connect to?
faqs.a: The Retaining Nut, DIN 3870 Heavy Series works with a DIN 2353 24° cone fitting body and a tube of the matching outside diameter. Ring, nut and body must be the same series and tube size, and the nut is ordered alongside the ring. Matching bodies are in the [DIN Hose Fittings](/c/din-hose-fittings) range.

faqs.q: How do I fit and seal the Retaining Nut, DIN 3870 Heavy Series?
faqs.a: Slide the nut and then the cutting ring onto a square-cut, deburred tube, seat the tube fully in the body and tighten the nut so the ring bites into the tube. Use the same series for ring, nut and body, and do not reuse a ring that has been taken up on a different tube. See our [guide to reusing fittings](/blog/reusing-fittings-in-a-rebuild).

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Retaining Nut, DIN 3870 Heavy Series and the Retaining Nut, DIN 3870 Light Series?
faqs.a: The Retaining Nut, DIN 3870 Heavy Series and the [Retaining Nut, DIN 3870 Light Series](/p/retaining-nut-din-3870-light-series) are separate listings with different sizes and specifications. The main difference is that the Retaining Nut, DIN 3870 Heavy Series is heavy series and the other is light series, and the two series are not interchangeable. Check the seat and series against your port before ordering.
